answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. It survives because finality only counts for established attestators, so a fresh cluster cannot push transactions until it proves honesty across many epochs. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a juniper as the anchor of the cost.
